To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the majority of the population in Europe and the USA are exposed to air pollution levels that are harmful to health; (ii) air pollution levels are highest in urban areas and are associated with increased morbidity and mortality; (iii) air pollution is associated with increased risk for cardiovascular diseases, respiratory diseases, and lung cancer; (iv) air pollution levels in Europe and the US are decreasing, but are not decreasing as fast as they should to achieve the WHO air quality guidelines.
